title: The Garuda Purana
author: vyasa
attributionNote: Ascribed to Vyasa, like the other Puranas, and compiled over centuries: its chapters on Vishnu's incarnations sit beside later additions on ritual, pilgrimage, medicine and the fate of the dead.
description: The Garuda Purana is the Purana of death, judgement and release, framed as a dialogue in which Garuda asks Vishnu about the fate of the soul. It describes the journey after death, the realms and their punishments, the funeral rites a son owes his parents, and, with them, cosmology, ethics, astrology, medicine and the worship of Vishnu and Shiva.
historicalContext: The text took shape mainly in Bengal and is recited beside the dead across northern India, which fixed its reputation as a book of mourning. It also preserves a great deal of practical lore: the diamond and gem chapters were consulted by jewellers, and its chapters on medicine circulated among physicians.
availabilityNote: Complete: the Sanskrit text of all three khandas as GRETIL publishes it, streamed from GRETIL at read time, one chapter at a time. This is the original Sanskrit, not a translation.
